mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-increase period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor market strengthening events since 2000, the 20-day forward return is non-positive (rolling IC < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% in a month suggests expanding domestic demand for capital goods, which typically precedes equity market optimism and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 15 similar monthly spikes in INDPRO since 2010 (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months indicates a supply-side easing, lowering growth expectations and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 70% of historical low-inflation episodes, 20-day forward returns are non-negative (rolling IC > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive (easing), the 60-day S&P 500 forward return tends to be positive due to anticipation of future rate cuts and easing credit conditions.
failure_condition: Over a 5-year window starting at each FEDFUNDS easing onset, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-onset period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising payrolls (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tight labor market, which can fuel equity risk appetite and produce positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS up while UNRATE flat or down over the same month
failure_condition: In 50% of tight labor market episodes since 1990, the 20-day forward return is non-positive (rolling IC < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 5% in a month suggests a supply shock that reduces growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: During 10 major INDPRO contraction episodes since 1980, the 5-day forward return was not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 1.5%, it often precedes a shift to a more accommodative policy, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days in non-recessionary regimes.
failure_condition: In 40 historical instances since 1980, the 20-day forward return was not positive when the 3-month MA crossed below 1.5% (p > 0.05).
